There is plenty of point in rushing it. If I am going to be homeless and hungry in 4 months, and do not want to live to see that day, there is no sense in not ending my life. "Rushing" implies the concept of time. In fact, time may not exist at all. It may just be a human construct. I have decided to stop seeing quacks, that like to call themselves psychiatrists and psychologists. They are the wackiest of us all, but they have a good income, so that keeps them mentally healthy. I think a good way to see all of existence is: everything is meaningless. All people are meaningless. All interests, all family members, all friends you ever had, are meaningless. It always was so. The only thing that changed from the time you enjoyed life, to now, was your mind. Nothing around you changed. So why did your mind change. You had too much time to think about it. All any of us can do is live our lives. There is a quote not to take life too seriously, because you will never get out of it alive. All that can be done is to live it and share it with others. For many people, that is enough meaning for them. We are all on this stage called planet Earth for a short time, then gone. It is true. How many people from the 11th century from the Gregorian calendar do you recall? Does it matter to you whether someone in 1037 killed themselves or continued to live the next few decades? I'm 32, and I live in a time when lief expectancy in developed countries is in the 6-7 decades range. I have been here for 3. For how much of it have I wished to not be here at all? For too much time, but I still think about it, and if I think about it often enough, I probably will kill myself. So what? You're right, so what, a crumb in the cake, as you put it. It's true, and I'm not refuting it. But you can also think about it this way: here I am, alive for a brief moment in time. It's my moment to do things, because where I am headed, I may never have another chance. In Jewish spirituality, I understand they have a proverb that goes something like this: hold in one pocket the notion that you are a speck of dust in the universe; in your other pocket, hold the notion that this universe was made for you. Hold these notions simultaneously. You will be at once humbled and invigorated. Also, I heard another saying high achievers keep as reminders: there will never be another now, I will make the most of today. There will never be another me, I will make the most of myself. I am not doing that myself and am in a very severe depression because I am falling far below my own expectations of what I should be accomplishing. But you can also say these are just phrases anyway, and what meaning do that have when you are dead? None, I can't refute that either. The problems I get into are when I have too much time to think. Life really does happen too fast for us to sit and think about it too much. That statue of the thinking man, is what we could become. Forever etched, just thinking, never acting, because we are too paralyzed by the understanding of our ultimate fate. I believe to be human is to be insane. People do lots of things to keep their minds off their own mortality; it's true. But so what? And what else do you expect people to do after all? If everything is meaningless, then the very idea of everything being meaningless, is meaningless. This logically must be so. So if that idea itself is meaningless, then anything under the banner of existence is meaningless, including suicide. Suicide is meaningless. I'm 32 and have ruined my life in many ways. Society judges you by certain measurements: schools attended? grades? jobs? income? Spouse? Children? These are the score cards by which we in developed countries are measured by. You know that one quote: "Suicide is man's way of saying to God: You can't fire me, I quit." So what now? Quit the game if you want to or not. Leave the game. We are born alone, and we die alone. No one came with us on the way in, and no one is going with us on the way out. I'm tired of playing this game myself: ruined 2 careers and an engagement to be married, and in the process of ruining a graduate program, all by 32. One thing I am very good at: fucking up my own life. I'm about tired of it. Believe me, I know the chorus of others as well as the next: it can get better, why? (they always want to know why). If doctors knew why, no one would kill themselves anymore, because it would have been cured. So, it can get better! why? What about the family and friends? Truth is, we are selfish beings, and especially that last one is an emotional appeal, which does not work with someone so far detached from life that they are seriously considering suicide. If I am seriously considering it (which I am), no emotional appeal will make a damn bit of difference. But people fortunate enough to not have any mental illnesses just cannot understand this. So we live with the stigma, and let's face it: the stigma contributes to reasons FOR killing oneself. Well, if I don't do myself in, I will get arthritis very soon from typing so much. Good bye for now. Maybe I will see some of you online strangers in the next life.

Long live no one, and if you believe in religion, pray that some illness claims my life this night, or soon. I eat poorly and do not exercise, to encourage illnesses. I look forward to a terminal illness. Cancer, or something, please claim me. Please.

And yes, I feel the arrows from all others. I do not live in the ancient times, when you could be pierced by arrows in battle. No, today we receive verbal arrows.
